internal.title: Incident Report: High Latency in Ad Service Resolved
internal.body:
At 12:10 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for high latency in the ad service, with p95 latency reaching 1.8 seconds, exceeding the 1-second threshold. Error rates remained low, indicating errors were not the cause. CPU utilization was observed to be very high at 98%, suggesting resource exhaustion as the primary factor contributing to the latency spike.

The on-call team diagnosed the issue and proposed disabling the adHighCpu flag at 12:30 UTC, which was approved and executed promptly. Following this action, latency metrics returned to normal levels (p95 latency dropped to 0.12 seconds), confirming recovery.

No recent deployments or active flags were identified as contributing factors. Memory and Kafka lag data were unavailable due to tool budget limits, but the evidence strongly supports high CPU utilization as the root cause.

This incident highlights the importance of monitoring CPU utilization closely and having responsive flag controls to mitigate latency issues quickly.
